coauthors.name: Hadi Hosseini
coauthors.affiliation: Penn State University, University Park, USA
coauthors.relevance_evidence: PI of the Penn State FAIR Lab and senior author on Khanna's whole line of work on LLM moral values and value alignment. arXiv 2506.00079 'Who Gets the Kidney? Human-AI Alignment, Indecision, and Moral Values' asks about LLM 'alignment with human moral values' and shows LLMs 'exhibit stark deviations from human values'; arXiv 2502.00313 'Distributive Fairness in Large Language Models: Evaluating Alignment with Human Values' examines 'whether LLM responses adhere to fundamental fairness concepts ... and investigate their alignment with human preferences', i.e. normative value alignment of LLMs rather than generic bias.

coauthors.name: Leona Pierce
coauthors.affiliation: Penn State University, University Park, USA
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Co-author on two LLM moral-values papers. arXiv 2608.05583 'The Judgment-Consequence Gap: LLM Moral Reasoning in Healthcare Decisions' (AIES 2026) states 'LLMs apply a systematically different moral framework than humans when responsibility and resource scarcity intersect'; also co-author of arXiv 2506.00079 on LLM alignment with human moral values in kidney allocation.

coauthors.name: John P. Dickerson
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Co-author of arXiv 2506.00079 'Who Gets the Kidney? Human-AI Alignment, Indecision, and Moral Values', which 'systematically evaluate[s] the behavior of several prominent LLMs against human preferences in kidney allocation scenarios' and argues for 'explicit alignment strategies for LLMs in moral/ethical domains' — LLM value alignment with human moral preferences.

coauthors.name: Xiyuan Wang
coauthors.relevance_evidence: Only seen on arXiv 2608.18631 'Preference Reasoning under Indeterminacy in Large Language Models', which is about epistemic/structural indeterminacy in social-choice reasoning, not cultural or moral values.

coauthors.name: Ronak Singh
coauthors.relevance_evidence: arXiv 2506.04478 on matching-market algorithmic reasoning with ranked preferences — combinatorial reasoning ability, no cultural or value dimension.

coauthors.name: Gonzalo Ballestero
